newsitem.title: USA: Galoob sees sales growth in second half.
newsitem.headline: Galoob sees sales growth in second half.

text.p: Galoob Toys Inc said Tuesday it expects sales growth across the board in the second half.
The company, reporting higher second-quarter earnings, said, "Obviously, we are very pleased to be $0.21 per share ahead of last year's earnings halfway through 1997."
Chief Executive Mark Goldman said, "We anticipate that a very full calendar of events will power broad-based sales growth in the second half of 1997."
Goldman said Galoob also expects to leverage sales growth with expanded margins in the second half.

"The video release and our new product introductions will be supported by massive advertising campaigns that will further increase consumer demand for our Star Wars product line throughout the important holiday season," he said.
Second quarter sales increased 6 percent, to $52.4 million from $49.2 million a year earlier.
Domestic sales increased 20 percent, led by the company's continuing Star Wars and Micro Machines lines and its new Men in Black line.
International sales fell 14 percent, reflecting a decline in the company's popular 1996 Sky Dancers and Dragon Flyz lines, as well as a generally weak European retail environment.
